sections.html: M. acora was described from the Rio Araguaia, a large tributary of the Rio Tocantins in Brazil. The imported fish come from the Rio Tocantins.

Flag cichlids (Mesonauta) from the Rio Tocantins in Brazil have a very variable basic pattern. This dark pattern, shown mainly when the fish are stressed or excited, is usually species-specific. Here, however, almost all specimens would belong to different species, which is not likely at all.

An examination of the described Mesonauta species makes it very likely that these imports belong to Mesonauta acora, a species known for its variable basic colours, and the stated distribution fits.

According to the revision of Mesonauta by Kullander and Silfvergrip, M. acora has a unique feature: 2-4 scales (most often 3) on the preoperculum. This is not visible to the naked eye in a living specimen, but can be seen on a photo.

M. acora has not been imported before, or at least the identification was not certain. It is said to be the rarest flag cichlid species in the hobby.

Kullander, S. O. & A. M. C. Silfvergrip (1991): Review of the South American cichlid genus Mesonauta Günther (Teleostei, Cichlidae) with descriptions of two new species. Revue Suisse de Zoologie v. 98 (no. 2): 407-448.
